title: What If a Gamma-Ray Burst Went Off Near Earth?

scenes.text: What if a gamma-ray burst went off nearby? Ten seconds could undo Earth's sunscreen.
Scientists modeled a burst within about six thousand light years of Earth. Only ten seconds of gamma rays would be needed.
Their models show up to half of the ozone layer could be destroyed within weeks.
Ultraviolet light would then pour in, endangering life on land and near the surface of oceans and lakes.
Plankton, the base of the ocean food chain, would be especially vulnerable. Deep-sea animals would stay shielded.
Five years later, at least ten percent of the ozone would still be gone. It is only a model, but it is a scary one.
